topics.definition: Consensus is the process by which distributed nodes agree on a single value or system state.
tips: Consensus is essential for distributed coordination.

topics.definition: Leader election selects one node to coordinate operations in a distributed system.
tips: Automatically elect a new leader after failures.

topics.definition: Raft is a consensus algorithm designed to be understandable while maintaining replicated logs.
tips: Uses leader election and log replication.

topics.definition: Paxos is a consensus algorithm that achieves agreement despite failures.
tips: More complex than Raft but highly reliable.

topics.definition: A quorum is the minimum number of nodes required to approve an operation.
Clock synchronization keeps timestamps reasonably aligned across nodes.
tips: Reduce clock drift for reliable ordering.

topics.definition: Split brain occurs when network partitions create multiple active leaders.
Use proven algorithms, monitor cluster health and maintain quorum.
tips: Maintain an odd number of nodes.
